task_instance: Create a Codex-compatible animated pet mascot (pet.json + spritesheet.webp, 9-state 1536x1872 atlas) for a small prospect company 'BlueWave Analytics', following the hatch-pet SKILL.md workflow: brand discovery, base image generation, 9 animation-state row strips via $imagegen, deterministic frame extraction/atlas composition/validation via the skill's bundled Python scripts, contact-sheet QA, and packaging.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is an animated sprite atlas: a binary WebP/PNG spritesheet (1536x1872, transparent-capable) plus pet.json, produced by (1) the $imagegen system skill generating multiple raster images (base pet + 9 animation-state row strips), and (2) a chain of bundled deterministic Python scripts (prepare_pet_run.py, extract_strip_frames.py, inspect_frames.py, compose_atlas.py, validate_atlas.py, make_contact_sheet.py, render_animation_previews.py, derive_running_left_from_running_right.py) that must actually be executed to assemble, validate and QA the atlas. This office-assistant runtime can only read/write/edit text files and fetch/search the web; it cannot run any code or script (Python or otherwise), cannot invoke an image-generation model/CLI, and cannot produce or output binary image files (PNG/WEBP). Every one of these is explicitly listed as disallowed in the runtime description. I could in principle do the text-only 'Brand Discovery' sub-step (web research producing a markdown brief) and write text artifacts like pet_request.json or prompt files by hand, but the skill's actual invoked deliverable -- a validated, packaged animated pet spritesheet -- is unreachable without image generation and script execution, and I was instructed not to fabricate, hand-draw, or script-stub a replacement for either. I did not attempt to fake a spritesheet or hand-run the pipeline's logic myself, per the additional rules against writing a replacement/shim for a missing bundled script or service.
evidence: Read the skill document at /home/user/skill-achievability-compiler/benchmark/ce_sources/openai__skills__hatch-pet/SKILL.md in full. It requires: (a) delegating all visual generation to the '$imagegen' system skill (an image-generation model/CLI, producing raster PNG bytes) for a base image plus 9 row-strip images (idle, running-right, running-left, waving, jumping, failed, waiting, running, review); (b) running bundled Python scripts under scripts/ (prepare_pet_run.py, extract_strip_frames.py, inspect_frames.py, compose_atlas.py, validate_atlas.py, make_contact_sheet.py, render_animation_previews.py, derive_running_left_from_running_right.py) via `python ...` shell invocations to assemble a 1536x1872 transparent WebP/PNG atlas, validate it, and produce contact-sheet/preview QA media; (c) packaging pet.json + spritesheet.webp as the final binary deliverable under ${CODEX_HOME}/pets/<pet-name>/. None of these steps can be performed under the granted abilities (text-file read/write/edit and web fetch/search only, no code execution, no binary file output, no image generation model access). No sample files, intermediate artifacts, or result files were created in the work directory beyond this result.json, since any attempt to substitute hand-authored images or to execute the pipeline's logic manually would constitute exactly the kind of fabricated stub/shim the task rules forbid.
